articles.en: Children growing up in war zones
body: Around the world, about one in five children now lives in an area affected by armed conflict.
全球约五分之一的孩子，如今生活在受武装冲突影响的地区。
War can interrupt their schooling, separate families, and leave deep emotional marks that last for years.
战争会打断他们的学业、拆散家庭，并留下持续多年的心理创伤。
The BBC discussion asks how ordinary people and communities can better protect and support these young lives.
BBC 这期讨论：普通人和社区可以怎样更好地保护与支持这些年幼的生命。

articles.en: Should we limit children's screen time?
articles.zh: 该不该限制孩子的屏幕时间
body: Many parents worry that phones and tablets take up too much of their children's day.
许多家长担心，手机和平板占掉了孩子太多时间。
Some countries have introduced rules to help families manage how long kids spend online.
一些国家已出台规定，帮助家庭管控孩子上网的时长。
The programme explores simple habits, like device-free meals, that may help without big fights at home.
节目探讨一些简单的习惯，比如吃饭时不碰设备，或许能减少家里的争吵。
tips: 不用电子设备的；无设备的

body: Disappointment shows up when things we hoped for do not turn out the way we expected.
当我们盼望的事没有按预期发生，失望就来了。
The BBC article shares small steps, such as naming the feeling and giving yourself time, to feel better.
BBC 文章分享了一些小方法，比如先说出这种感受、给自己一点时间，会好受些。
It also reminds us that setbacks can teach lessons we would never learn from easy wins.
它还提醒我们：挫折能教给我们一些顺境里学不到的东西。

articles.en: Why young people love the past
body: A growing number of young people are looking back at older music, fashion and films for comfort.
越来越多年轻人回头听老歌、穿老式衣服、看老电影，从中寻找安慰。
Experts say nostalgia can steady us when today feels fast, uncertain or overwhelming.
专家说，当现在让人觉得太快、太不确定、太累时，怀旧能让我们安心。
The BBC piece looks at why 'the good old days' feel safer than an unpredictable future.
BBC 这篇文章探讨了：为什么'过去的美好'比无法预测的未来更让人有安全感。
tips: 令人不知所措的；压倒性的

articles.en: Beating the fear of speaking English
articles.zh: 克服开口说英语的害怕
body: Many learners feel clever and funny in their own language but quiet and boring when they speak English.
许多学习者用自己的母语时又机灵又幽默，一说英语就变得安静、无趣。
BBC teachers suggest starting with short, low-pressure chats instead of perfect grammar or big speeches.
BBC 老师建议：先从简短、没压力的闲聊开始，别一上来就追求语法完美或长篇大论。
With small daily tries, the awkward feeling fades and confidence slowly grows.
每天小试一下，那种尴尬感会慢慢消失，信心也一点点长出来。
